note: Survey (Zhang, arXiv 2512.08455) states it is conjectured that Behrend's lower bound is the best upper bound for r_3(N), and Elsholtz-Hunter-Proske-Sauermann (arXiv 2406.12290) list Kelley-Meka/Bloom-Sisask exponent 1/12 -> 1/9 vs lower exponent 1/2 as an open gap. The exact N exp(-c sqrt(log N)) question is the stated open conjecture, so not new.

Same open Behrend-vs-Kelley-Meka gap: whether exp(-Theta(sqrt(log N))) is the truth is a stated conjecture/open problem (Zhang survey). Note the lower-bound side (beat Behrend's constant) was already done in arXiv 2406.12290 (constant 2*sqrt(log2(24/7)) < 2*sqrt2), but the asked o(sqrt(log N)) improvement is open.

Asks for exponent gamma<1/2 construction or the matching upper bound; this is the same open gap between Behrend (exponent 1/2) and Bloom-Sisask/Kelley-Meka (exponent 1/9), stated as open in the survey and in arXiv 2406.12290, which only improves the constant in the sqrt(log N) shape.

The first part (construct sets with constant c < 2*sqrt(2 ln 2)) is answered by Elsholtz-Hunter-Proske-Sauermann, arXiv 2406.12290: r_3(N) >= N 2^{-(C+o(1))sqrt(log2 N)} with C = 2*sqrt(log2(24/7)) < 2*sqrt2 (Behrend's constant), so the premise 'no construction has improved this constant' is false. The ambitious kappa=0 part remains the open exponent question.

Alexeev-Mixon (arXiv 2510.19804) give size-5 counterexample {1,2,4,8,13}; the 'least size of a non-extendable Sidon set' (3<=s<=5) is posed as open in arXiv 2604.25214 (marked withdrawn; it proposes {0,1,3,11} as a size-4 non-extender with computational evidence only, and says an MO answer by Mueller covered it, which I could not open). Question is therefore known and unresolved/unverified.

Part (a), does every 4-element Sidon set extend to a perfect difference set, is the known size-4 question from the Alexeev-Mixon follow-up literature (arXiv 2604.25214, withdrawn, claims candidate counterexamples such as {0,1,3,11} but unverified). Part (b), the density of primes q, was not found.

Sub-question (2), whether all Sidon sets of size <=4 extend, is the known size-4 question (arXiv 2604.25214, withdrawn, with unverified candidate counterexamples). The density formulation via c_k = limsup E_k(N)/S_k(N) and its k->infinity behaviour was not found.

Pilatte's paper (arXiv 2303.09659, Introduction) says a simple modification of the proof should give a B_h[1] set that is an asymptotic basis of order 2h-1 for h>=2, answering a question of Kiss-Sandor; this addresses (as a sketch) Q2 (g(h)<=2h) but not Q1 (order h+1 for h>=3). Exact question not found.

Pilatte's paper recalls Erdos's open conjecture of Sidon sets with S(x) >> x^{1/2-eps} (best known x^{sqrt2-1-o(1)}, Ruzsa) and builds a Sidon basis from Ruzsa/Cilleruelo-type sets; a Sidon basis of order 3 with density x^{1/2-o(1)} would imply the open Erdos conjecture, so it is a strengthening of a known open problem, but this exact density question was not found.

Same as P-233237: dense (x^{1/2-eps}) Sidon sequences are Erdos's open conjecture (best known exponent sqrt2-1, Ruzsa, per Pilatte arXiv 2303.09659); the Sidon-basis-of-order-3 density question itself was not found stated.

Pilatte's paper (arXiv 2303.09659) notes probabilistic p(n)~n^{-2/3} sets are almost surely not order-3 bases and uses much denser Ruzsa-type sets, but no source posing a thin Sidon basis with R_S(n)=n^{o(1)} or O(log n) was found.

Prendiville (arXiv 1409.8234) gives quantitative bounds for x, x+d^k, x+2d^k (k-th power differences, square case included) of loglog type, and Green-Sawhney (arXiv 2411.17448) get N exp(-c sqrt(log N)) only for the two-point square-difference problem. Kelley-Meka-strength for 3-APs with square difference was not found stated or solved; no source posing this exact question was found.

Same landscape: Prendiville's homogeneous polynomial Szemeredi (arXiv 1409.8234) covers x, x+d^2, x+2d^2 with loglog-type bounds; Green-Sawhney (arXiv 2411.17448) give exp(-c sqrt(log N)) for x, x+d^2. The 3-point quasipolynomial question and the lower-bound question (2) were not found as stated.

Jain-Pham-Sawhney-Zakharov (arXiv 2405.08650) state the explicit bound n^{c/loglog n} versus Erdos's O(log n), and say a construction with sigma_A <= exp((log N)^eps) or better 'would be interesting'; explicit polylog is thus a recognized gap but not posed in this exact form (the paper does not state it as a formal open problem).

Same paper (arXiv 2405.08650) records the gap between explicit n^{c/loglog n} and probabilistic O(log n) and Kolountzakis's poly(n)-time derandomization, and says exp((log N)^eps)-type explicit bases would be interesting; the weaker version exp((log n)^{1-delta}) is essentially this recognized direction, but the exact strongly-explicit polylog question was not found as a stated problem.

Same as P-b38cfb: arXiv 2405.08650 gives the explicit bound n^{c/loglog n}, notes Erdos's O(log n) probabilistic bound, and expresses interest in explicit exp((log N)^eps) or better; the stated polylog / exp((log n)^{1-delta}) questions are close variants, not found verbatim.

arXiv 2601.18507 proves there is a basis with r_A(n) > eps*log n (eps=15/(512 log 2)) containing no minimal subbasis, which answers the 'is c_3>0' sub-question (yes); the exact values of c_3, c_2 and whether c_2=c_3 are not determined (arXiv 2603.03472 calls the 1/log(4/3) constant 'mysterious', Erdos-Nathanson Question 4 style linkage).

arXiv 2601.18507 shows C_min is positive (a basis with r_A > eps log n without minimal subbasis), but does not decide whether C_min < 1/log(4/3) or equal to C_split; arXiv 2603.03472 discusses the Erdos-Nathanson constant without determining it. Exact values appear open; exact question not found as stated.

Related results: Erdos-Nathanson threshold 1/log(4/3) for both properties, arXiv 2601.18507 (minimal-subbasis threshold is not 1/log(4/3) at least in the sense that bases with r_A > eps log n and no minimal subbasis exist, so gamma_3 > 0), arXiv 2603.03472 (independence of the three properties for slower growth). Whether gamma_2 = 1/log(4/3) or gamma_2 = gamma_3 was not found settled.

Borwein-Choi-Chu poster computes the finite version exhaustively for bounds k=3..6 (maximal element of a finite k-basis 8, 40, 52, 264; ordered-pair convention, slightly different N definition), and Dubickas (EJC 2012) notes r_A(n) cannot stay in [1,5] or [1,7] for all large n; finiteness for every fixed R is the open Erdos-Turan conjecture. The explicit-growth exp(R^c) question was not found.

Same circle: Dubickas (EJC 2012) records that ordered r_A(n) cannot all lie in [1,5] (and [1,7]), i.e. N_k finite for k<=7, so N_8 is right at the edge of the known results; the finite-interval computations for small k are in the Borwein-Choi-Chu poster. Finiteness of N_8 itself is not stated as settled; exact phrasing and the growth-rate question not found.

This is the 'Ruzsa number' R_m of Z_m (Chen; ordered counts): known R_m <= 128 for all m (arXiv 2607.06167), earlier 192/288/5120, and Sandor-Yang R_m >= 6 for m >= 36 (per arXiv 2407.02344), so the existence of a uniform constant is known; the sharp liminf/limsup values (sub-questions a-c) were not found settled.
